assessment.nobel_worthiness: Estimating demand and supply in differentiated-product markets with endogenous prices, and dynamic industry models, changed empirical industrial organisation. The methods are standard in merger analysis, antitrust and regulatory work, with broad influence across fields.
assessment.attribution: The Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes demand framework is the clearest core. Pakes also led the dynamic oligopoly and entry/exit estimation work. Bresnahan, Benkard, Levin and Reiss are important but more peripheral to a three-person award.
assessment.maturity: The core work dates from the 1990s and has about thirty years of validated use, so it is highly mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to include Bresnahan or the dynamic-games contributors over Levinsohn.
Some of the contribution is a method, and the committee may prefer awards tied to a substantive discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work formalised how lobbying and special-interest politics shape trade policy. They also built the endogenous-growth, innovation and trade framework. The work transformed how international trade theory is joined to political economy and growth, and it has had lasting influence.
assessment.attribution: Grossman and Helpman are a long-standing joint pairing, with the 1994 protection-for-sale model and the book on innovation and growth in the global economy as the central outputs. Credit is clear and well matched to two laureates.
assessment.maturity: The work is three decades old and has been extensively tested and extended, though empirical testing of the protection-for-sale model is mixed.
uncertainties: How far the 'protection for sale' predictions hold empirically.
Helpman also appears on another candidate, so there is overlap in the longlist and a possible question about how his credit is distributed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki and Moore's collateral-constraint model of credit cycles showed how small shocks are amplified and persist through asset prices and borrowing limits. This is a foundational mechanism in macro-finance and underlies much post-2008 work.
assessment.attribution: The 1997 Kiyotaki-Moore paper is clearly the origin of the mechanism and is a natural two-person credit. The financial accelerator is a related but separate strand (Bernanke-Gertler, Gilchrist), and Bernanke has already been recognised. Gertler and Gilchrist are therefore left out.
assessment.maturity: The idea is nearly thirty years old and is widely used, and its relevance was reinforced by the financial crisis.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would treat Gertler and Gilchrist as essential to credit-cycle theory.
The model is stylised, and the empirical evidence is mostly indirect.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: It showed that misallocation of resources across firms can account for much of the cross-country gap in TFP and income. This reoriented the research agenda in growth and development accounting and links micro data to aggregate outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow's 2009 paper is the main source of the quantification. Restuccia and Rogerson's parallel work is also important, and only Restuccia is credited here, so the attribution is not fully clean.
assessment.maturity: The paper is about seventeen years old and has a large follow-up literature, though its findings are debated, notably on measurement error and the size of the effects.
uncertainties: Sensitivity of the magnitudes to measurement error and to how distortions are inferred.
Credit sharing with Restuccia and Rogerson, who is not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work gave political economics a systematic framework. It covers how electoral rules and constitutions shape fiscal policy and how state capacity relates to development. The research is influential across public economics, political science and development.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini's book and papers, together with Besley's work on state capacity and political agency, form a coherent joint programme. Credit is spread across a trio and is fairly clear.
assessment.maturity: The programme has run for about thirty years and is well established. Some empirical identification of constitutional effects remains disputed.
uncertainties: Identification of causal effects of constitutions and electoral rules.
My own field proximity (political economy of growth) could bias my view, so I flag it rather than treat it as evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Constructing long-run series of top income shares from tax data opened up the empirical study of inequality, which was previously poorly measured. The work has had large intellectual and policy impact, with measurement as a fundamental contribution.
assessment.attribution: The Piketty-Saez top income series is the core measurement contribution. Zucman's later offshore-wealth and distributional-accounts work is significant but more recent and was reached through a separate line, and I leave it out of a two-person award.
assessment.maturity: Top-income work dates from the early 2000s, while the wealth-distribution and offshore components are newer and more contested.
uncertainties: Methodological disputes over the wealth-concentration estimates and the treatment of taxes and transfers.
Whether the committee views the contribution as measurement rather than theory.
Piketty's broader theoretical claims are contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work on technology, tasks and trade exposure reshaped understanding of labour-market polarisation and the local effects of import competition. It had wide influence on empirical labour economics and policy debates.
assessment.attribution: The China shock papers (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) and the task framework are distinct contributions. The task-based theory that is central to the first strand is partly attributed to others not credited here, such as Levy, Murnane and Acemoglu.
assessment.maturity: The core papers are from about 2003 to 2016. Long-run follow-up evidence is still accumulating and effects have been qualified.
uncertainties: Attribution of the task framework to people outside the credited names.
Whether the findings hold up under later re-estimation and identification critiques.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities, together with the Taylor rule, underlies the way central banks analyse monetary policy. Its practical and conceptual importance is very large.
assessment.attribution: Credit is highly diffuse. Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and others are all defensible, and capping the award at three forces difficult exclusions.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been in use for decades. Its performance in recent inflation episodes and its use of representative agents continue to be debated.
uncertainties: Selection among many plausible laureates with no clear natural subset.
Overlap with earlier prizes for related monetary and macro contributions.
